Package de.l9g.scm.oauth2.plugin

package de.l9g.scm.oauth2.plugin
OAuth2/OIDC authentication for SCM-Manager (authorization code flow with PKCE).

How the plugin is wired into SCM-Manager

There is no explicit registration anywhere: SCM-Manager scans the plugin for classes annotated with @Extension and for JAX-RS resources, everything else is instantiated by guice. The entry points are:
  • OAuth2AuthenticationResource - the two http endpoints of the flow, /api/v2/oauth2/auth and /api/v2/oauth2/auth/callback
  • OAuth2Realm - shiro realm, turns an OAuth2Token into an authenticated subject
  • OAuth2GroupResolver - tells the core which groups a user belongs to, used for authorization
  • ForceOAuth2LoginFilter - servlet filter for the optional forced single sign on
  • AfterLogoutRedirectToIdp - hook of the core logout resource, performs the RP-initiated logout
  • IndexConfigurationEnricher - adds the links oauth2Login and oauth2Config to the index resource, which is how the react frontend learns that the plugin is configured
  • OAuth2ExternalAuthenticationAvailableNotifier - lets the core know that users may exist without a local password
  • ConfigurationResource - REST endpoint of the administration ui

Login flow

  1. The browser calls GET /api/v2/oauth2/auth?from=/repos (button on the login page, or a redirect of the ForceOAuth2LoginFilter).
  2. StateStore creates an AuthorizationRequest: a random state, a Pkce verifier and the sanitized target url. The state is additionally written to the browser as StateCookie.
  3. The response is a redirect to the authorization endpoint, which EndpointResolver either takes from the manual configuration or from the discovery document fetched by DiscoveryClient.
  4. The identity provider authenticates the user and redirects back to /api/v2/oauth2/auth/callback?code=...&amp;state=....
  5. The callback verifies that the state matches the state cookie of this browser and consumes it (single use), then hands the authorization code to LoginHandler as OAuth2Token.
  6. subject.login(token) ends up in OAuth2Realm, which delegates to AuthenticationInfoBuilder - the place where everything comes together (see below).
  7. LoginHandler issues the access token cookie of SCM-Manager, the callback redirects to the target url and invalidates the state cookie.

What happens on every login

AuthenticationInfoBuilder is the single place which orchestrates the following steps, so start reading there:
  1. OAuth2RestClient exchanges the authorization code for tokens and fetches the userinfo claims.
  2. UserInfoMapper maps the claims to a user, UserMigration merges it with an account which may already exist under the same name.
  3. The groups of the claim plus the roles read by AccessTokenRoleReader are passed through GroupNameSanitizer and stored in the GroupStore (the source of the OAuth2GroupResolver).
  4. GroupSynchronizer creates missing groups and updates the memberships, AdminGroupSynchronizer assigns or revokes the global administrator permission.
  5. The id token is kept in the IdTokenStore for the logout.

Logout flow

The core logout resource logs the subject out and then asks every LogoutRedirection extension for a redirect target. AfterLogoutRedirectToIdp builds the url of the end session endpoint with id_token_hint (taken from the IdTokenStore) and post_logout_redirect_uri, so the identity provider terminates its own session without a confirmation prompt and sends the browser back.

Configuration

OAuth2Configuration is the single configuration object of the plugin, persisted as xml by OAuth2Context and edited through the de.l9g.scm.oauth2.plugin.config package. Read it with context.get(); it is never null, an unconfigured instance simply returns the defaults with enabled == false.

Conventions worth knowing

  • Elevated privileges: while a login is processed the subject is not authenticated yet, so every access to users, groups or permissions runs inside AdministrationContext.runAsAdmin.
  • Failures: anything which is not the authentication itself (group synchronization, admin permission, logout hint) must never break the login, therefore those parts log and continue.
  • Error responses: values received from the identity provider are only written to the log, never reflected to the browser.
  • In memory state: StateStore and IdTokenStore are deliberately not persisted and therefore not cluster wide; a restart only means that a running login has to be repeated and that a logout happens without hint.
